what: a modelled M10 thread on a d10 shaft running down to a d16 shoulder: it reaches the shoulder at every angle, the collar whole
method: the shaft's lower end is a shoulder (the d16 collar lies past it, in the groove's way), so the groove runs on past its plane and is trimmed there; the top end is free, the groove runs out into the air. Every slice of the shaft along the axis then loses the same, whatever its height: V = pi 8^2 10 (the collar) + pi 5^2 25 - (25/P) V_turn, V_turn = 2 pi int r m(r) dr one turn of the groove within the shaft (m as in 001); the centre of mass from the two parts' moments (the threaded part's at its middle, the screw averaging every meridian alike). Tolerance 0.05%: the groove is SMLib's exact screw sweep; a groove running a pitch into the collar (the old free-end overrun) removes 0.9% more, and one stopping clear of the shoulder leaves its last turn uncut, 0.26% more material
